title: Calendula sitz bath
subtitle: A soothing herbal sitz bath of Calendula officinalis for postpartum perineal care and vulval irritation
excerpt: Calendula sitz bath is a strong infusion of dried calendula flowers, cooled to a comfortable temperature and added to a shallow bath or sitz bath bowl. Traditionally prepared for postpartum perineal care, vulval irritation, and minor external inflammation. One session uses 50 g of dried flowers in 1 litre of water; the soak lasts 15 to 20 minutes. Dried calendula keeps 12 months in a tin.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), marigold entry, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Calendula officinalis L., flos (2008, revised 2020), open access.

glossaryTerms.definition: A shallow bath in which only the hips and buttocks are submerged, used in herbal and conventional practice for perineal and vulval care. The name comes from the German 'sitzen', to sit.

content.text: is a strong infusion of dried calendula flowers, cooled to skin-comfortable temperature and poured into a sitz bath bowl or shallow bath. A gentle, soothing external preparation long used in postpartum care for perineal soreness after a vaginal birth, and for vulval irritation or external inflammation. The orange-gold flowers soften and cool the area. A 15 to 20 minute soak once or twice a day.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place 50 g of dried calendula flowers in a large saucepan. Pour 1 litre of just-boiled water over the flowers. Cover and steep for 20 minutes.
Strain through a sieve into a large jug, pressing the flowers to extract the liquid. The infusion should be a rich amber-orange.
Allow to cool until the liquid is warm but comfortable on the inner wrist, not hot. Pour into a sitz bath bowl or a shallow bath.
Sit with the perineal area submerged for 15 to 20 minutes. Pat dry gently with a clean soft towel afterwards.
Once or twice daily for postpartum or acute care. For ongoing vulval irritation, once daily for up to two weeks then reassess. If there is no improvement or symptoms worsen, see a doctor.
Dried calendula flower stores 12 months in a sealed tin. Prepare the infusion fresh for each session. do not store the strained liquid.
When not to use this remedy
Do not use if you have an Asteraceae allergy. See a doctor for vulval discharge, unusual odour, or significant pain. These symptoms need a diagnosis before any herbal treatment.
